title: Basis of Charge for a Day of Skiing on a Lift Ticket Order
content:
What a day on a Lift Tickets order costs turns on how the day was bought.

| What is bought | The basis of the charge |
| --- | --- |
| A day bought at the window on the day | the product's window price |
| A day bought at least the product's advance period ahead of the ski date | the product's advance price |
| A product sold as a block of days | the product's block price, whatever the dates the days are later used on |

The advance period is counted in whole calendar days between the order date and the ski date.

## The age band

The age band of the holder sets a percentage of the adult price. The child, youth, senior and super senior bands each take their own share, and the band is judged on the holder's age on the ski date rather than on the age at the order date.

## The holiday surcharge

A day scanned inside a published holiday period adds the product's holiday surcharge. That surcharge is raised when the day is drawn, not when the order is placed, so an order bought outside a holiday period for a date inside one carries the surcharge at the lift.

## Counting the advance period

The count runs in whole calendar days from the order date to the ski date. On a product whose advance period is 5 whole calendar days — a figure taken for this illustration only — an order dated the 1st of a month for a ski date on the 6th of the same month stands 5 whole calendar days ahead, and so is placed at least the advance period ahead. An order for that ski date dated the 3rd stands 3 whole calendar days ahead, and has not been placed at least the advance period ahead.
